text:
maya: heads/kvdim perf anomaly on qwen-1.2 16k runs — saw ~22% tail latency increase when we flip on paged-KV. anyone else seeing this?

tom: saw that on my run too. short sequences are fine, but long context tails blow up.

li: I sampled with nvprof and perf — hotspots look like `fused_gemm_kv` and a new `kv_copy_page` kernel. attaching quick flame: `fused_gemm_kv` -> aten::linear -> kv_copy_page.

maya: repro command i used:
```
profiler run --model qwen-1.2 --batch 8 --seq 16384 --mode throughput --trace flame
```
output excerpt: "p99=128ms -> 156ms after paged-KV enabled"

alex: interesting, we changed the kernel-choice pivot last week to prefer the wide-f32 kernel for >48 kv-dim. maybe that's regressed when num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads (GQA).

li: hypothesis: paged layout interleaves per-head kv pages which causes unaligned loads for the preferred kernel, leading to increased memory traffic and fragmentation (lots of small memcpy ops). also RoPE scaling introduces extra elementwise ops just before kv writeback. :thinking:

maya: quick experiment: switch kernel pivot back to legacy f16-fused for qwen-1.2 on A100S and run the same workload. results: p99 126ms (baseline 128ms) and p99 with paged-KV 131ms (was 156ms). so kernel pivot matters.

tom: good catch. question: do we need a per-model kernel pivot that is kv-layout-aware (i.e., prefer kernel version that assumes contiguous per-head layout when using paged-KV)?

li: yes — propose adding runtime predicate: if paged_kv && (num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads) then prefer the narrow-vector copy-friendly kernel. Also add a microbenchmark for the kv_copy_page kernel to detect fragmentation thresholds.

infra-bot: perf test job queued: `perf/qwen-1.2/paged-kv-kernel-pivots/1768888900`

alex: also saw a perf regression correlated with RoPE scaling op we added. aten::addcmul shows up between attention and kv write. that op is cheap per element but multiplied by 16k sequences => high memory bandwidth. maybe fuse RoPE scaling into the kv write kernel?

maya: plan: 1) add kernel-pivot predicate based on paged_kv and head mismatch, 2) add microkernel for kv_copy_page to do head-contiguous memcopy when fragmentation small, 3) try fusing RoPE scale into the write path, 4) run canary perf job and A/B compare. I'll open a PR with patch + benchmark.

tom: ping me on the PR, i'll run CI perf harness on dedicated nodes. :rocket:

li: extra note — batching heuristic: adaptive batcher should prefer smaller batches when median seq > 8k but p99 > 12k to reduce kv page churn. we can add that parameter to the adaptive policy.

maya: thanks — moving to action items. will post PR link and perf numbers here when ready.
